notes: Format fixture (mw-e22.3), not shipped: Oswin Brand at the forge (story bible §5.7). Exercises class-gated options (knight, thief), a locked option that shows its reason (the tally stick), a persuasion check with modifiers and a failure that continues the story, and effects. The real conversation is written under E39.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: WHAT? No. WHAT? Oh, a customer. Speak up, I'm deaf in the one ear and you're standing on it.

options.text: I need a real blade, and I can't pay for it yet.
My armour has seen better days.
I hear you sell lockpicks. For miners.
Do you know this tally stick? The notches stop halfway down.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: A commission. A REAL one. Swords for nobody, forty years, and now this. Pay me when you're back. Come back.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: No. WHAT? No. Credit's how smiths end up making spoons. Come back with coin.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: A knight! In my forge! Give me that, give it HERE. No charge. Don't tell the miners.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Picks, yes. For miners. Very stubborn locks, down the mine. Very stubborn miners.

nodes.speaker: oswin
nodes.text: Hazel, notched by a man who counted every bucket. Mine work, that. Keep it safe. Someone should keep counting.
